items.rationale: All 6 bounded members are Jazzy-rendered API-detail panels under the generated docs tree, including the mirrored docset copies. Their repeated height/section/declaration/parameter markup is renderer scaffolding around distinct API documentation; refactoring the emitted HTML would be overwritten and would not improve the Swift source.

All 286 bounded members are Jazzy symbol rows in generated documentation files, with Apple symbol anchors, token links, and renderer-added declaration notes; the same structures also occur in docset mirrors. This is high-volume presentation-template output, so moving it out of bare default removes noise without hiding a source-level refactoring.

All 8 bounds are generated Jazzy method-detail div/section panels, repeated between ordinary documentation and docset output. The common abstract/declaration/parameter skeleton belongs to the documentation renderer while the prose and signatures describe different APIs, leaving no maintainable extraction in these emitted files.

All 72 members are bounded generated-documentation fragments (parameter containers, table rows, or prose paragraphs) under Jazzy pages and their docset copies. Similarity comes from stable renderer markup around API-specific text, not handwritten program structure that a user should consolidate.

All 98 members are Jazzy-emitted parameter sections or parameter rows across generated API pages, including mirrored docset output. The table hierarchy is a presentation template and the cells carry different parameter semantics; changing generated HTML is neither durable nor a useful application refactoring.

All 32 source bounds are generated Jazzy parameter-table rows in the docs tree and docset mirrors. Their shared td/code/em/description form is renderer-owned markup around different parameter names and descriptions, so no actionable source extraction would be hidden.

All 1,644 members are bounded td cells from Jazzy-generated parameter tables under the docs tree. The repeated code/em cell shape is an extremely small renderer leaf replicated across API pages and docset copies; presenting it as a default refactoring candidate would be pure generated-output noise.

All 140 members are generated Jazzy parameter containers, rows, or short list blocks, with matched copies in generated docset pages. They share the renderer's documentation layout while describing different API parameters, so editing or extracting from the emitted HTML would not be a durable refactoring.

All 48 bounded members are Jazzy declaration panels or complete item blocks containing generated symbol anchors, highlighted Swift declarations, and documentation layout. The clones reflect page generation and docset mirroring, not duplicated implementation logic that should stay on the bare default surface.

All 52 bounds are Jazzy-generated parameter sections or table rows in API documentation and its docset copies. Their shared graybox/table scaffold is renderer output around distinct parameter prose; consolidating the emitted fragments would be ineffective and would not improve production code.

All 72 members are generated Jazzy symbol-link blocks carrying Apple anchors, token links, and renderer-added extension/default-implementation notes. The uniform div/code structure is navigation metadata emitted across docs and docset mirrors, with no actionable source-level helper to extract.

All 24 bounded members are Jazzy-generated aside/note blocks in API pages and their generated mirrors. Although some prose is repeated, these are emitted documentation nodes rather than maintainable implementation units; a clone refactoring against the HTML would be overwritten and misleading.

All 6 members are complete Jazzy initialization task-group or item panels containing generated anchors, declarations, and parameter presentation, with mirrored copies. Their common structure is renderer composition around different initializers, so it is not an actionable handwritten-code clone.

All 196 members are generated breadcrumb paragraphs, one per Jazzy API page, using the same breadcrumb/carat template and including docset duplicates. This is canonical site-navigation output whose repetition must remain in the generator template, not be refactored in emitted pages.

All 6 bounds are Jazzy-rendered declaration or item panels for related encode methods, complete with generated anchors and highlighted Swift declarations. They are documentation renderings of distinct protocol/class APIs and mirrored outputs, so demoting the emitted similarity does not conceal an implementation refactoring.

All 16 members are generated Jazzy abstract blocks or parameter rows in API pages and docset mirrors. The repeated markup is renderer-owned while each bound carries API-specific descriptions, leaving no durable refactoring in the generated artifacts.

All 8 members are Jazzy-generated parameter-section divs with the standard graybox/table scaffold, repeated in generated documentation copies. The structure is presentation boilerplate rather than duplicated executable behavior, so it should not occupy the bare default surface.

All 10 bounded members are generated Jazzy parameter-section divs, including exact documentation/docset mirrors. They render parameter names and prose through the same fixed table template; modifying the generated HTML would not be a meaningful or persistent refactoring.

All 78 source bounds are Jazzy-emitted parameter rows in generated API pages and corresponding docset pages. Their common row layout is renderer boilerplate around differing option/parameter documentation, so hiding this generated-output clone does not hide actionable code work.

All 16 members are generated Jazzy abstract-description divs for API methods, duplicated into docset output. The repeated paragraph container is renderer structure while the long descriptions are API-specific; there is no useful extraction to perform in these emitted pages.

Both bounded members are body-free ANTLRErrorStrategy contracts: a Swift protocol and the corresponding Java interface expose parallel signatures and documentation but no reusable implementation. Cross-language contract parity cannot be consolidated into a shared helper, so demotion would not hide an actionable refactoring.

Both members are identical declaration-only TypeScript UploadState aliases inside separate Prettier formatter fixtures. Extracting and importing a shared alias would change the fixture inputs and couple independent formatting cases without removing implementation duplication, so the family is not pragmatically actionable.

All 4 members are body-free TypeScript constructor-signature declarations in one Prettier formatting fixture, deliberately varying interface versus type-alias syntax and generic formatting. A shared base or alias would erase the syntax cases under test rather than improve implementation design.

Both members are small, body-free State type aliases local to separate Zustand test files. Sharing this test-only shape would add an exported test helper and coupling for four declarative lines while offering no implementation reuse, so moving it from bare default does not conceal worthwhile refactoring.
